scope: Actual native Rust library execution of the fixed-scope StorageSession on real SQLite on three platforms, plus the standalone storage regressions. Library-level evidence only: no Tauri command, TypeScript binding, application restart or editor.
observations: Linux and macOS run 33 core harness cases (12 unit + 3 session integration + 18 storage integration); Windows runs 31 (16 storage integration) because two Unix-specific permission/path cases are not applicable there.
The Unix-only cases are not a Windows waiver: Windows ACL, reparse-point and hard-link policy remain open gates.
The eight session unit cases include cancelled accepted writes, shared idempotent close, capacity retention until completion and final-reference drop; none uses test doubles.
Immediate temporary-directory removal after awaited close passes on Windows, confirming the complete SQLite pool shutdown fix also covers the session path.
limitations: External revocation gives a stable UNAUTHORIZED close result; disk or flush failure injection is not covered because the lower-level close returns no error.
Read, merge and output budgets, aggregate sessions, snapshot transport and runtime shutdown are still open.
Async Drop is best effort and needs a live runtime.
